title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Mendoza and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show the grape, often Malbec, the region, Mendoza, and increasingly a sub-region or GI, like Valle de Uco, Luján de Cuyo or Gualtallary. Altitude is often printed. Argentina requires 85% of a named grape. Reserva and Gran Reserva have minimum ageing rules for reds: 12 and 24 months.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Malbec is the wine of the asado, Argentina's barbecue: beef ribs, steak, chorizo and morcilla, blood sausage, with chimichurri, a herb and garlic sauce. Cabernet Franc suits lamb and herbs; Bonarda suits pizza and pasta; Torrontés suits empanadas. Serve Malbec at 16 to 18 degrees.

steps.prompt: Which sauce is a classic with Malbec and steak?
steps.explanation: Herbs, garlic and vinegar suit Malbec's fruit.

steps.body: Many Mendoza labels print the vineyard's altitude. Higher usually means fresher, more floral and more structured.

steps.prompt: Argentina requires 85% of a named grape on the label.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show grape, sub-region and often altitude
Malbec is the wine of the asado
